deductions: Tightness and organisation −3: “agree a specific next action” in Conversation path repeats the closing instruction to “agree who will do what and when.”
Clarity −2: “qualified, owned follow-up” is abstract here; the ownership process appears later in Qualify and close.
Evidence and confidentiality −4: “Built for uptime” can sound like a performance promise beside the instruction that product claims still need confirmation.
Continuity −7: “Before the visitor leaves, state the action, owner and timing” conflicts with the later step where Peter and Eerin assign the action to a salesperson.
Clarity −6: “owner” does not distinguish the person promised to the visitor from the salesperson assigned after the event.
Actionability −6: The two ownership steps leave a rep unsure whom to name when agreeing the next step.
Continuity −6: The normal scan note asks for an “agreed next step” but omits the owner and timing required in Qualify and close.
Actionability −7: Unlike the failed-scan note, the normal saved record need not contain timing or an owner, which can weaken the promised hand-off.

overall_findings: Sections 03 and 04 do not meet the 95-in-every-dimension threshold because the agreed owner and timing are not carried consistently into the saved lead.
No critical confidentiality or lead-save failure is visible in sections 00–04. Section 05 was not supplied, so roster and timetable preservation cannot be assessed.
